g_rules.text: Tweet 1 is the hook: bold promise, surprising claim or emotional statement that stops the scroll
Hook has no 'Thread:' or '[1/N]' numbering
Hook stands alone as a great tweet
Hook formula menu: Result+Timeframe, Bold claim, Contrarian, Story opener, Listicle, Behind-the-scenes, Curiosity, Challenge
Context tweets 2-3: establish credibility, define problem, set expectations
One idea per value tweet, never two
Start each value tweet with a bold statement or number
Concrete examples, not abstract advice
Vary value tweet format: tips, stories, data
Each tweet valuable/understandable in isolation
Value tweet pattern menu: numbered tip, lesson+story, do this not that, stat+insight
Tweet N-1 is a scannable numbered TL;DR recap
Summary ends with a save prompt ('Save this thread...')
Final tweet is always a CTA
Pair follow CTA with retweet request
CTA menu: follow, 'Retweet the first tweet', reply question, link, engage
Links only in last tweet or first reply, never the hook
Max 15 words per sentence
Line break between every sentence, one thought per line
No walls of text; split or cut dense tweets
Fragments are fine, they add punch
Vary rhythm: alternate short punches and slightly longer lines
Emojis sparingly, 0-2 per tweet max
Never start the hook tweet with an emoji
No multiple emojis in a row / cluttered emoji text
Arrow (flow) and check (lists) as thread markers
Digits, not words, for numbers
Specific numbers beat round ones
Start value tweets with '1.', '2.' for scanability
Use dollar amounts and percentages to grab attention
Length tiers 5-7/8-12/13-15, optimal 8-12, avoid 16+
Story Thread template beats
Listicle Thread template
Contrarian Take template beats
Tutorial Thread template beats
Case Study Thread template beats
CTA matched to the thread's goal
No tweet exceeds 280 characters
Thread delivers on the hook's promise
Output section 1: Thread Outline, bullet plan of the arc
Output section 2: Full Thread, each tweet numbered with character count, as posted
Output section 3: 3-5 alternative hook variations
Output section 4: posting time, all-at-once vs delays, recommended first reply, first-hour engagement plan
Posting time based on audience timezone
Thread teaches, inspires or entertains (ideally two)
